calc.description: calc_v1 (panel genesis mint 2026-10-13): parameter block copied VERBATIM from the served h100_broad_v1_calc_v13 registry doc (iqm_alpha 0.16666, 15-min slot grid from 2026-08-28, carry-forward 72h, pre-smoothing 1h, attendance eta 0.5, population-floor scaling) so this lane is the same engine generation as the six live lanes; METHODOLOGY.md is the binding contract. RECORD: raw-observatory snapshots from the 2026-08-27 genesis (first day of the 15-min record). TIER SCREEN: allow-list on-demand only. NO parity leg: no predecessor series. SKU SET: {A100} (the catalog files 40GB and 80GB parts under one sku; the per-seat rules below do the split). 80GB RULES (verified 2026-10-13 against the collector code, fixtures and the engine's own screen functions). (1) require_memory_gb 80 -- FAIL-CLOSED on the observation's top-level memory_gb_label (absent or different -> ineligible, counted memory_label_absent / memory_label_mismatch): verda, civo, crusoe, lambda, runpod, e2e, hyperstack, coreweave, ovh, deepinfra -- every collector that emits the field (int 40/80 on verda, civo, lambda, runpod, e2e; 80 on crusoe, hyperstack, coreweave, ovh, deepinfra). It is the ONLY 80GB rule on those seats: label tokens, string extras and declared grants that would have said the same thing are deliberately not stacked (one rule per axis; the memory field is the authoritative one, and a label/field contradiction must not be hidden by a second rule). (2) label require_tokens, fail-closed, where no memory field exists: massedcompute and lium '80GB' (their 40GB parts self-label 40GB), sesterce_console '80G' (its 80GB rows are 'A100_80G'; its bare 'A100' rows are 40GB). (3) extra_require part_number 'B95907' -- oracle (OCI's only A100-labelled rental row; the 40GB BM.GPU4.8 is the chip-less 'Compute - GPU - E3' row, unmapped by design). DISCLOSURE: extra_require is FAIL-OPEN on an ABSENT key -- an oracle row recorded without extra.part_number would be admitted unscreened (the collector sets the key on every price-list row today; a collector reshape dropping it would print whatever row is cheapest). NOT SEATED at genesis: vast (no memory on its record before the 2026-10 capture change; book 40GB-dominated), gpuai (ruling), the sesterce pricing page (bare 'A100' From floors). MARKETPLACE STATISTICS: lium via lium_vwm_book_floor. MEMBER EXTRA SCREEN: runpod Secure-only via extra.cloud. CURRENCIES: ovh (FR subsidiary) bills EUR -> ECB lane; e2e INR row held out mechanically. RECORD FACTS (47-day persistence scan 2026-10-12, canonical slot): direct seats printed on 46-47 of 47 days, lium 34 of 47 (thin -- expect thin_book hold-outs). LIVE-PROBE FIGURES at mint (2026-10-13 capture, screened, NOT lane prints): seats 0.89 (deepinfra) to 4.00 (oracle).

description: A100 80GB BROAD hourly panel (the SKU-expansion scoping record (fcp METHODOLOGY.md); rulings 2026-10-12: 80GB only, one panel). Underlying: a BLENDED rate across A100 80GB capacity as each provider sells it (PCIe and SXM4 mixed) -- composition is the instrument, as on H100-BROAD. MEMORY is the screen: 40GB rows run 25-40% cheaper within a provider. Every seat whose collector emits the top-level memory_gb_label (ten seats) carries the FAIL-CLOSED require_memory_gb 80 rule; the four seats whose collectors emit no memory field screen through their own labels (massedcompute, lium '80GB'; sesterce_console '80G') or a structured part number (oracle, extra_require -- fail-OPEN on an absent key, disclosed in the calc description). 14 members (11 direct + runpod and massedcompute + lium statistic seat), weight floor 1.25%, claim floor 8. NOT seated at genesis: vast (its record carried no memory before the 2026-10 capture change and its book is 40GB-dominated -- a later mint once memory-labelled captures accumulate), gpuai (ruling 2026-10-12), sesterce pricing page (bare 'A100' From floors of unknown memory). Selection over the raw-observatory record; captures nothing.
